At Central Adelaide (CALHN), we're shaping the future of health through excellence in clinical care, research, and innovation. As South Australia's largest health network, we deliver exceptional, safe and connected healthcare - for our patients, our community, and our people.

With more than 17,000 dedicated employees, every day at CALHN presents an opportunity to make a real impact-not because it's expected, but because our values guide us to be our best. Find out more about CALHN sites and services, our stories and the opportunities to be part of CALHN.

Join a supportive Mental Health team where you'll help create seamless administrative support that enables quality client care. You'll manage appointments, maintain accurate records, build strong relationships and provide essential support across multiple sites within Western Services.

Key Responsibilities

- Maintain client records and data accuracy
- Schedule appointments and update calendars
- Respond to phone, email and counter enquiries

- Experience in administration, reception or customer service

Part-Time Position-s

7-day week rotating roster

0600-1400hrs & 1200-2000hrs shift pattern

We're building for the better!

By 2036, more than 150,000 patients will look to us for healthcare every year.

At Cabrini Health we champion community, compassion and career fulfilment. Our teams are united by the shared purpose of making a meaningful contribution to exceptional, patient-centred care in well- resourced, world class facilities that inspire you to perform at your best and continuously grow professionally.

Join a team that makes a meaningful impact every day.

Cabrini Health is seeking an organised, proactive and collaborative Staffing Allocations Clerk to support efficient and safe staffing across our hospital. This is an excellent opportunity for someone who thrives in a dynamic environment and enjoys working closely with clinical leaders to ensure high-quality patient care.

About the Role

The Staffing Allocations Clerk plays a vital role in ensuring our clinical areas are appropriately staffed to meet daily operational demands. You will be responsible for coordinating Nurse Bank and Pool staffing, responding to staffing requests, managing agency engagements, and maintaining accurate systems and documentation.

Working closely with the Hospital Coordinator and reporting to the Clinical Services Director - Clinical Operations, you will support the smooth and safe delivery of care across Cabrini Malvern.

Key Responsibilities

Receive, document and action contingency staffing requests from clinical areas

Allocate Nurse Bank, Nursing Pool and ward redeployment based on roster needs

Liaise with nursing agencies when internal cover cannot be provided

Ensure accuracy of staffing systems including UKG (Dimensions) and ShiftMatch

Maintain shift records, data and documentation as per Cabrini procedures

Coordinate onboarding schedules for new Nurse Bank & Pool staff

Manage inbound and outbound calls, providing timely and professional communication

Uphold Cabrini's Mission, Values and Behaviours that Matter

About You

We are looking for someone who is organised, calm under pressure, and excellent at communication.

You will bring:

Strong clerical and administrative skills

Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, Outlook)

Experience managing or operating databases and-or staffing systems

Excellent interpersonal skills and the ability to work collaboratively

A customer-focused approach with a commitment to high-quality service

Ability to maintain confidentiality and work within professional boundaries

What we offer:

Salary packaging: up to $15,900 tax-free each year, plus $2650 meal & entertainment card benefits

Convenience: Vibrant Malvern location, close to local shops, cafes and public transport

Travel Perks: Myki Commuter discounted fares

A commitment to health and well-being initiatives including discounted access to a wide range of gyms, pools, and fitness facilities through Fitness Passport

Access to a range of retail offers, discounted hospital services and savings on eligible private health fund services

To view the full position description click here 

Enquiries should be directed to: Hammish Manning Clinical Services Director - Clinical Operations on 9508 1302

Apply early! This role may close sooner than the listed closing date if we find the right candidate - so don't wait to get your application in.

Does this sound like your new role? Bring your skills and enthusiasm to Cabrini Health and help optimise the patient experience and health outcomes for our community.

Cabrini Health acknowledges the importance of creating a work environment that is welcoming, safe, equitable and inclusive for people of all backgrounds and abilities. Inclusion is core to our mission.

As part of our commitment to Reconciliation and Closing the Gap in employment related outcomes, we encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples.

Working for Cabrini

Cabrini Health is a Catholic, private, for-purpose health service located in Melbourne's southeast. Inspired by the mission and ethic of care of the Cabrini Sisters, providing quality, compassionate care to our community for more than 75 years.

There is something special about Cabrini Health. Our highly skilled staff and specialists incorporate clinical research, innovative models of care and state-of-the-art technology to deliver the best possible care and outcomes for our patients. We demonstrate our mission to serve our community through outreach programs that support asylum seekers, provide healthcare in rural communities and in underdeveloped countries.

Our size, reputation and growth strategy ensure genuine opportunities for our people to learn, grow and realise potential.

Our values: Compassion - Integrity - Courage - Respect

MANDATORY FOR ALL NEW STAFF TO CABRINI

Employment with Cabrini Health will be based on satisfactory background checks such as professional references, National Police Check, vaccinations for annual Influenza plus a Working with Children Check (WWCC) may also be requested. Vaccination for COVID-19 is highly recommended.    Click here to Apply now →

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Your Role at St John of God Midland Public Hospital 

St John of God Midland Public Hospital provides high-quality public and private services to people living in the east metropolitan and Wheatbelt regions. Midland is one of our busiest hospitals, with demand for public services consistently increasing every year, making it a dynamic and fast-paced environment to work in.

St John of God Midland Hospital is seeking a motivated and highly capable Colorectal Fellow - Senior Registrar to join our established and progressive colorectal unit for a comprehensive full-time 12-month fellowship, starting February 2027.

Supervised by four experienced colorectal surgeons, the Fellowship is designed to develop expertise in the assessment, management and surgical treatment of the full spectrum of colorectal disease. The Fellow will gain extensive hands-on experience in advanced laparoscopic and minimally invasive colorectal surgery, while developing skills in perioperative decision-making, multidisciplinary care coordination, leadership and clinical research.

The SJOG Midland Colorectal Unit is a high-volume service performing more than 150 colectomies annually and is recognised for its collaborative approach to patient care, working closely with Gastroenterology, Gynaecology, Oncology and Psycho-Oncology services. The faculty maintains strong national and international professional links, is actively involved in research and education, and includes surgeons who currently hold or have held leadership positions within CSSANZ, RACS and the WA Colorectal Cancer Collaborative.

Fellowship Highlights

Dedicated colorectal outpatient clinics.

Exposure to more than 100 elective and emergency public colectomies annually.

Elective benign and malignant colorectal surgery, including inflammatory bowel disease.

Participation in colorectal and emergency on-call services.

Proctology and anal manometry experience.

Access to both colonoscopy and upper GI endoscopy lists with colorectal surgeons and gastroenterologists.

Exposure to advanced laparoscopic, minimally invasive and robotic surgical techniques.

Private assisting opportunities, including complex colorectal and gynae-colorectal cases.

Supervision and mentoring opportunities with SET and non-accredited surgical trainees.

Research, Leadership and Innovation

The Fellow will have access to the unit's unique Colorectal Cancer Database (CIC), incorporating PROMs, and GSTAR, the colorectal morbidity and outcomes database, providing excellent opportunities for research, quality improvement, presentations and publication. Dedicated colorectal nursing, data management and project support enable meaningful academic output throughout the Fellowship.

The role also provides valuable leadership experience through teaching and supervising junior medical staff, participating in audit and morbidity review processes, and contributing to clinical governance and service improvement initiatives.

The unit continues to lead innovation in Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) and is actively developing overnight colectomy pathways, providing exposure to contemporary models of perioperative colorectal care.

The 2027 Fellowship is part-funded through a Medtronic educational grant and is seeking CSSANZ accreditation for the 2028 training year.

This Fellowship offers an outstanding opportunity for advanced colorectal training within a high-volume, academically active and progressive colorectal service.

To be successful in this role

You will Hold current registration as a Medical Practitioner with the Medical Board of Australia (AHPRA) and be an advanced Royal Australasian College of Surgeons (RACS) SET trainee, Fellow, or possess equivalent surgical training and experience.

You will be able to demonstrate strong clinical and procedural skills within colorectal surgery, general surgery, or a comparable surgical environment and have a genuine interest in pursuing advanced training and a career in colorectal surgery.

Above all, you place patients at the centre of your practice and are committed to supporting our Mission and Values in every aspect of your work.

We can offer you:

Salary: $188,817 - $198,142 per annum, plus 12% superannuation

Professional development allowance $16,747 pro rata per Annum if part time

A welcoming and supportive culture

Salary packaging up to $18,550 on a range of benefits such as mortgage, rent, meal entertainment, holiday accommodation or other everyday living expenses as well as options to salary package benefits above the FBT cap on items such as:

Novated leasing 

work related expenses

self-education and

additional superannuation

A healthy work-life balance through flexible work options, additional purchased leave and well-being programs

Employee discount on St John of God Hospital & Medical Services and Private Health Insurance

Employee support through our dedicated free Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

Opportunities for education and professional development

* All applicants are asked to submit a covering letter (of no more than two (2) pages) demonstrating how you meet the requirements of the role

For enquiries about this position, applicants should contact Mary Theophilus, ph. 9462 4488

Agency applications will not be considered

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Orthopaedic Surgery, Trainee Unaccredited Position, Hawkesbury District Hospital

Employment Type: Temporary Full Time (01-Feb-2027 up to 2 years)
Remuneration: $117,745 - $147,664
Hours Per Week: 38
Requisition ID: CAM30078

The Trainee will effectively be required to assess trauma patients appropriately in the Emergency Department and then carry out basic trauma care in the operating theatres under consultant supervision. The Trainee will be an important part of a unit, also charged with the supervision of interns and junior medical officers. Preparation of clinical material for weekly department meetings will be necessary, as well as participation in quarterly audit meetings including the collection and presentation of data. Teaching and training of junior staff as well as nursing and allied health may be required during the year.

What you'll be doing

Assessing trauma patients appropriately in the Emergency Department and then carry out basic trauma care in the operating theatres under supervision.

Assisting with elective work performed at the hospital.

Reviewing and managing patients in outpatient clinics including preadmission clinic for elective surgery, orthopaedic fracture and wound review clinics, virtual and telehealth clinics; and a range of elective clinics including the high risk foot clinic.

Initial assessment of the patient: this consists of ensuring a complete and documented comprehensive patient history, physical examination and the formulating of a management plan and ordering appropriate investigations.

Participating in overtime rosters and an after hour oncall roster including weekends.

 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 

 

Essential requirements

MBBS or equivalent, currently registered with the Medical Board of Australia in an appropriate registration category.

At least three years' postgraduate experience in public hospital service (or equivalent).

Demonstrated clinical practice as a registered medical practitioner in the last 2 years in a setting appropriate to the needs of the position.

Sufficient clinical experience in order to undertake the key accountabilities for this role

This position is subject to an appropriate supervision level which can be supported by the health agency. If the incumbent's registration conditions include supervision requirements, the level of supervision must be able to be supported by the health agency for this role.

Valid Working with Children Check, cleared National Police Check.

To be employed by NSW Health you are required to provide evidence of vaccination to comply with the NSW Health Occupational Assessment, Screening & Vaccination against Specified Infectious Diseases Policy, this includes any amendments made from time to time.

Selection criteria

Qualifications and experience commensurate with the Essential Requirements for the role.

Demonstrated ability to work independently within a supervised complex clinical environment utilising excellent clinical skills, judgment and expertise.

Advanced verbal, written and interpersonal skills, with the capacity to vary communication style in line with the understanding of the needs of diverse audiences.

Demonstrated ability to prioritise workloads and display a flexible approach to meet changing situations in a demanding and unpredictable clinical environment.

Demonstrated commitment to continuing professional development and self-education.

Demonstrated commitment to quality improvement, patient safety and risk management.

Need more information? Click here for the Position Description. 
Find out more about applying for this position. Please ensure you attach your curriculum vitae to your submission.

Dr Haren Nandapanan at haren.nandapalan@health.nsw.gov.au
